groups.heading: ADVANCED OBJECTION
items: postulation, non-apprehension and tradition to its three accepted means of valid knowledge (pramāṇas).
This economy creates a burden: imperceptible Primordial material nature (prakṛti) and Conscious witness (puruṣa) cannot simply be asserted.
Samanyato-drsta inference must reach entities never presented as ordinary sense-objects.
Carvaka attacks the unobserved universal relation, while Nyaya grants inference but proposes atoms and Lord (Īśvara) as a more economical explanation.

groups.heading: COMPARATIVE NUANCE
items: Samkhya replies that material continuity, guna-patterns and the objectifiability of
experience jointly require one material root and a distinct witness.
Empirical cognition occurs through the inner instrument.
Sensory mind (manas) coordinates, ego-maker (ahaṃkāra) appropriates and determinative intellect (buddhi) determines.
